answer: Dune-Phase Whisper Echo: agents emit sparse 64–256 B whisper beacons at jittered intervals seeded by a public dune schedule; peers log arrival-time residuals and return delayed echo probes, then score per-agent timing entropy and cross-identity autocorrelation over 24 h. Sybil clusters from one scheduler share residual patterns, so they fail or must run independent clock/egress jitter, sustain always-on cover traffic, and absorb false-positive retries—cost scaling with identity count.
